name: Paney Homestead
reason: Parks SA page names Paney Homestead and Old Paney Heritage trail as early station relics inside Gawler Ranges NP (rule 1, 1 source).
objection: It is part of the larger Gawler Ranges National Park; a ruin with a short look and one source.

name: Conical Hill
reason: Not named on the Gawler Ranges park page or any counted source; a hill inside a larger park (rule 3).
objection: Has 4.6k page views, but the views belong to a different Conical Hill possibly.

name: Gawler Ranges Wilderness Safaris
reason: Operator of 4WD tours, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: Two counted sources list it, but both list a business.

name: Lake Gairdner National Park
reason: Parks SA page: Australia's third largest salt lake with 200 islands, free entry, open daily; obvious natural draw (rules 1-2).
objection: Access is via a 34 km station track and a key from Mt Ive station, so many visitors cannot easily reach it.

name: Pildappa Rock
reason: Wikivoyage and eyrepeninsula.com: striking granite wave-wall inselberg, walk to the top for views (rules 1-3).
objection: Dirt road access, mostly a caravanner stop; a similar rock formation as others nearby.

name: Polda Rock
reason: Wikivoyage and eyrepeninsula.com: recreation reserve with picnic area, birdlife and a walk around the rock base, free (two counted sources).
objection: Ordinary picnic reserve; near duplicate of the other granite rocks.

name: Tcharkulda Rock
reason: Wikivoyage: 'probably the most photographed rock in the area' with boulders, trails and facilities; two counted sources.
objection: Only a short stop for many visitors.

name: Ucontitchie Hill
reason: eyrepeninsula.com (one source) calls it a bare-rock dome of international geological significance; free, open.
objection: Single source, 32 km off the highway, short visit; similar to Pildappa and Tcharkulda.

name: Australian Farmer Granite Sculpture
reason: Wikivoyage and eyrepeninsula.com: large granite sculpture at Wudinna's Telecentre, the town's signature roadside icon (quirky landmark).
objection: Ten-minute stop beside the highway; minor as art.

name: Wudinna Granite Trail
reason: Wikivoyage: 9 km walking/bike trail from Wudinna to Little Mount Wudinna through Polda Rock reserve (one source).
objection: Partly duplicates Polda Rock; a connector trail rather than a distinct sight.

name: Big Galah
reason: Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula lists the Big Galah at Kimba (Halfway Across Australia): a classic big-thing roadside icon (rule: quirky icons).
objection: A ten-minute photo stop beside a shop.

name: Whites Knob Edward John Eyre Sculptures
reason: Wikivoyage: explorer statues on a scenic hill 4 km from Kimba (one source, link dead).
objection: Single old listing marked dead link; short visit; minor public art.

name: Workshop 26 Kimba Creative Quarter
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: not-for-profit women's art collective with a gallery and shop, free; called a must-do (one source).
objection: Limited opening days; closer to a shop/gallery than a sight.

name: Kimba Gawler Ranges Historical Society
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: Kimba Museum on early agricultural life, from $5, open Wed-Fri (one source).
objection: Small local museum with limited hours and a single source.

name: Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists a visitor centre and museum on the iron-mining history that helped build Australian steel (one source).
objection: Listing has no detail and only opening hours; a small-town museum.

name: Iron Knob Mine Tours
reason: Wikivoyage lists weekday mine tours at Iron Knob, the mine that fed the steel industry; the place is the mine (one source, 2015).
objection: Tours are an operator activity and the listing dates from 2015, so they may no longer run.

name: Middleback Range
reason: No counted source names it as a place to go; a range of working iron-ore hills.
objection: Wikipedia page views of 1.7k show interest, but not as a visitor stop.

name: Corunna Station
reason: No counted source; a working pastoral station.
objection: Possible station-stay interest, but not a source-named stop.

name: Wangaraleednie Monument Ruins
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: a historical grave site and monument; a minor memorial with a short visit (rule 3).
objection: A tourism board does list it as free and open.

name: Lake Greenly
reason: No counted source names it; a salt lake with nothing for a visitor to do.
objection: Only 239 views and no tourism listing.

name: Greenly Beach
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: popular swimming and surfing beach an hour from Port Lincoln, bluffs and reef; second-tier beach stop.
objection: One source and a camping-oriented council page; beach is similar to others on the coast.

name: Redbanks Beach
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: pristine beach north of Arno Bay for swimming, surfing and walking; second-tier beach.
objection: One source; ordinary local beach.

name: Observation Hill Lookout
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: Cleve bushland hill with a lookout and Silver Daisy protection (one source).
objection: Small local hill, one source, short visit.

name: Federation Hill Lookout
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: 360 degree views from the Darke Peak Ranges, easy 260 m walk (one source).
objection: Accessed through private property and a short walk; single source.

name: Cummins Mosaic Trail
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: self-guided trail of mosaic artworks through Cummins, free (one source).
objection: Street art around a small town; little to fill half an hour, one source.

name: Black Stump
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: Cowell's giant Black Stump between two hotels, a quirky roadside icon with a story (quirky icon rule).
objection: A prank stump; ten-minute stop.

name: May Gibbs Tree
reason: A 1973 memorial monument to the author; a minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: Famous author link might draw fans.

name: Bonnie the Clydesdale Sculpture
reason: Small local metal sculpture in Cleve; minor public art with no distinct draw.
objection: Tourism board lists it, but as part of a Cleve sculpture set.

name: Reggie the Wedgie Sculpture
reason: Small local metal sculpture on Cleve's main street; minor public art.
objection: Might count as a quirky icon, but the listing is minimal.

name: Fishermens Memorial
reason: A minor memorial (rule 3).
objection: Possible port-lincoln waterfront interest.

name: Salted Barrel Sauna
reason: Operator selling a sauna experience, not a place.
objection: It is a destination experience for some.

name: Painted Studios
reason: An artist's studio open by request only; not open to the public (rule 2).
objection: Gallery online.

name: Gulf and Ranges Trail
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: 4 km hiking and cycling loop at Crag Point near Whyalla with geology signage and views of Spencer Gulf and the ranges (one source).
objection: Short loop, one source; neighbours other Whyalla trails.

name: First Nation Trail
reason: Follows the same Fitzgerald Bay / Point Lowly shore as the Freycinet Trail, with signage only; overlaps a trail judged separately (rule 3).
objection: Interpretive First Nations content is of cultural value.

name: Freycinet Trail
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: 12 km coastal hiking, cycling and driving trail along Fitzgerald Bay to Point Lowly (one source).
objection: Linear coast route partly overlapping other trails and Point Lowly; one source.

name: Heritage Trail
reason: An urban creek-side shared path in Port Lincoln ending at a playground; not a visitor draw.
objection: Local council lists it in the tourism board site.

name: Saltmarsh Trail Eight Mile Creek
reason: Two short virtual-guided mangrove boardwalk trails near Whyalla; minor local nature walks with a single source.
objection: Mangrove and samphire ecosystem is unusual and tourism board listed.

name: South Head Walking Trail
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: Venus Bay walk with dolphins, sea lions, sea eagles and southern right whales May-October (wildlife named).
objection: One source; short coastal walk.

name: Locks Well Walk
reason: eyrepeninsula.com: 283-step wooden staircase down to a West Coast beach with lookout and sunset photography; a known Elliston-area stop.
objection: One tourism-board source; the beach is a fishing-focused spot.

name: McKenzies Landing
reason: An old wooden landing platform seen from the road; a short roadside look, minor (rule 3).
objection: Heritage curiosity near Denial Bay.

name: Davenport Creek
reason: Candidate coordinates are in Utah, USA, and no evidence a creek reserve is a visitor stop.
objection: Listed on a tourism board page.

name: Port Gibbon
reason: The source is a playground page; a coastal camp settlement with no named sight.
objection: Coastal camp could be a swimming and fishing stop.

name: Eyre Peninsula Railway
reason: eyrepeninsula.com Port Lincoln Railway Museum: heritage station building with memorabilia, from $6, open Wednesday afternoons only (one source).
objection: Very limited hours; candidate is named for a railway rather than the museum.

name: Port Lincoln Marina
reason: A marina is a facility, not an attraction.
objection: Waterfront stroll and boat watching.

name: Boston Bay Wines
reason: One of many cellar doors; no source singles it out as a destination estate.
objection: Port Lincoln's only winery region.

name: Cape Bauer Oysters
reason: Oyster farm operator, a business not a place.
objection: Farm tours are popular.

name: Streaky Bay Oyster Barn
reason: Seafood operator/shop, not a distinct sight.
objection: Eat-at-source oyster stops are a regional draw.

name: Port Lincoln Smokehouse
reason: A food shop, not a visitor sight.
objection: Local seafood fits the region's identity.

name: Nautilus Arts Centre
reason: eyrepeninsula.com lists it as Port Lincoln's arts centre with gallery spaces (one source).
objection: A performing-arts venue first; entry and exhibits vary.

name: Middleback Arts Centre
reason: Whyalla performance venue; shows are events, a venue with nothing standing to see (rule 4).
objection: A community art gallery could be open.
